summary: The implementation adds startswith/endswith methods that work correctly for matching strings and ignoring non-strings. However, the hashval used for query caching does not include the prefix/suffix parameter, causing different queries (e.g., startswith('Al') vs startswith('Alx')) to have identical hashes and be considered equal. This breaks query caching and query combination.

checks.claim: startswith/endswith correctly match strings and ignore non-strings
checks.evidence: python -c test shows non-strings (None, numbers, missing fields) don't match; case-sensitive matching works

checks.claim: Query caching/hash is broken - different prefixes produce same hash
checks.evidence: python -c test shows where('name').startswith('Al') == where('name').startswith('Alx') returns True and they have identical hashes

findings.text: startswith hashval ('startswith', self._path) doesn't include the prefix parameter, causing different prefixes to have identical hashes
endswith hashval ('endswith', self._path) doesn't include the suffix parameter, causing different suffixes to have identical hashes
